attributes.name: description
attributes.description: What the set is for.

attributes.name: model_purpose_code
attributes.description: The purpose the set was assembled for.

entities.name: feature_set_member
entities.title: Feature Set Member
entities.description: Membership of a feature in a feature set - the many-to-many bridge between feature_definition and feature_set. Modelled relationally so features are shared, not duplicated per set.
entities.grain: One row per feature per feature set.

attributes.name: feature_set_member_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the membership row.

attributes.name: feature_set_id
attributes.description: The feature set.

attributes.name: feature_id
attributes.description: The feature that is a member of the set.

entities.name: model_asset
entities.title: Model Asset
entities.description: A governed analytical or machine-learning model as a business asset - what it is, what it is for, who owns it and where it is registered. Versions, features, scores and monitoring hang off it. This is how the semantic layer governs AI the way it governs data.
entities.grain: One row per model asset.

attributes.name: model_id
attributes.description: Stable identifier for the model asset, owned by the data layer.

attributes.name: name

attributes.name: model_type_code

attributes.name: description
attributes.description: What the model does, in business language.

attributes.name: owner_role
attributes.description: Accountable owner of the model, as an org role.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Platform or registry the model is managed in.

entities.name: model_monitor_metric
entities.title: Model Monitor Metric
entities.description: A monitoring measurement for a model version over a period - performance and drift tracked through time. This is what turns "the model is governed" into evidence: whether the champion still earns its role.

attributes.name: model_monitor_metric_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the monitoring measurement.

attributes.name: model_version_id

attributes.name: monitor_metric_type_code
attributes.description: The kind of metric measured.

attributes.name: period

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Monitoring system the measurement originates from.

entities.name: model_score
entities.title: Model Score
entities.description: A score a model version produced for a business object - the atomic output of a model. Polymorphic by subject_kind (policy, quote, claim, party) so one governed table holds every score and each traces to the version that made it. Business-facing signals such as a fraud signal consume scores; they are not the same thing.

attributes.name: subject_kind_code
attributes.description: What kind of object the score is about.

attributes.name: scored_at
attributes.description: When the score was produced.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Serving system that produced the score.

entities.name: model_version
entities.title: Model Version
entities.description: A specific trained version of a model asset - when it was trained, on what frame, how it scored, and its serving role. Every score and decision cites a version, so a decision is always reproducible to the exact model that made it.

attributes.description: Value of the headline evaluation metric at training time.

attributes.name: promoted_on
attributes.description: Date this version became champion, where applicable.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Registry the version is tracked in.

entities.name: legal_entity
entities.title: Legal Entity
entities.description: A legal entity in the group's structure and the reporting hierarchy that connects them. entities.name: consent

entities.name: data_subject_request

entities.name: party

entities.name: underwriting_decision

entities.name: vehicle
entities.title: Vehicle
entities.description: Motor-specific detail for an insured object of type VEHICLE. This is the model's typed-satellite pattern: the generic insured_object stays lean, and object types that need depth get a satellite entity - vessels, buildings surveys or cyber estates would follow the same shape.

attributes.description: Whether the vehicle is enrolled in a telematics programme.

entities.name: policy_event
entities.title: Policy Event
entities.description: One immutable lifecycle event of a policy - the append-only spine of policy administration. attributes.name: event_id
attributes.description: Deterministic identifier for the event (seeded), stable across rebuilds.

attributes.name: policy_id
attributes.description: Policy the event concerns.

attributes.name: sequence_no

attributes.name: policy_event_type_code

attributes.name: event_ts

attributes.name: effective_from

attributes.name: reverses_event_id

attributes.name: event_source_system_code

attributes.name: actor_type_code

attributes.name: actor_id

attributes.name: premium_delta

attributes.name: sum_insured_delta

attributes.name: coverage_change_note

attributes.name: reason_code
attributes.description: Reason the event occurred, e.g. non-payment, insured request (payload).

attributes.name: prior_event_hash
attributes.description: Hash of the prior event in the chain; empty for the first event.

attributes.name: event_hash
attributes.description: Hash of this event chained onto prior_event_hash. Recomputing and comparing the chain proves no event was altered or removed.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: System of record the event row is stored in.

quality.name: event_period_ordered

quality.description: An event cannot cease to have effect before it takes effect.

entities.name: policy_version
entities.title: Policy Version

The current policy is the version where is_current is true; a claim attaches to the version in force at its loss date.

attributes.name: policy_version_id
attributes.description: Identifier for this policy version.

attributes.name: policy_id
attributes.description: Policy this is a version of.

attributes.name: policy_number

attributes.name: legal_entity_id
attributes.description: Carrying legal entity as at this version.

attributes.name: underwriting_year
attributes.description: Underwriting year of account as at this version.

attributes.name: renews_policy_id
attributes.description: Prior policy this term renewed from, as recorded on the policy.

attributes.name: version_no
attributes.description: Version number within the policy, increasing as events change state.

attributes.name: valid_from

attributes.name: valid_to

attributes.name: is_current

attributes.name: created_by_event_id
attributes.description: The event that created this version.

attributes.name: line_of_business_code

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Policy currency as at this version.

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: System of record the version is stored in.

quality.name: version_period_ordered
quality.rule: valid_to IS NULL OR valid_to >= valid_from
quality.description: A version cannot be superseded before it takes effect.

entities.name: renewal_chain
entities.title: Renewal Chain
entities.description: Links a policy to its predecessor and to the stable chain of all renewals of one original risk. This is what makes "customer since 2019, seventh renewal" answerable, and what the renewal loop and the customer dimension hang off. It formalises the policy renews-from linkage as first-class data.
entities.grain: One row per policy, placing it in its renewal chain.

attributes.name: renewal_chain_id
attributes.description: Identifier for the chain-membership row.

attributes.name: policy_id
attributes.description: The policy placed in the chain.

attributes.name: chain_id
attributes.description: Stable identifier of the risk across all its renewals.

attributes.name: predecessor_policy_id
attributes.description: The prior policy this one renewed from; empty for the first term.

attributes.name: renewal_number
attributes.description: Position in the chain; 0 for new business, 1 for first renewal, and so on.

entities.name: derived_factor
entities.title: Derived Factor
entities.description: The factor level and contribution applied to a specific quote or policy - the rating build-up made concrete. Summing the contributions reconstructs the quoted premium, so a price is always explainable to the factors that made it.

attributes.name: contribution
attributes.description: Premium contribution of this factor, in the quote currency.

entities.name: rating_engine_config
entities.title: Rating Engine Config
entities.description: A versioned rating configuration for a line of business - the base rate and the model version behind it, effective-dated. This is what a quote's rating provenance points to, tying a premium to a governed model version.

attributes.name: rating_engine_config_id

attributes.name: line_of_business_code
attributes.description: Line of business the configuration rates.

entities.name: rating_factor
entities.title: Rating Factor
entities.description: A factor used to rate a line of business - the named driver premium responds to (e.g. vehicle group, flood band, mileage). Factors are data, so a rating build-up is inspectable rather than buried in engine code.

attributes.name: rating_factor_id

entities.name: rating_factor_feature

entities.name: rating_factor_level

entities.description: A level of a rating factor and its relativity - the value a factor can take and what it does to premium. Levels are effective-dated so a historic quote can be re-priced with the relativities in force when it was made.

entities.name: appetite_rule

entities.name: product

views.name: cession_bordereau_line
views.title: Cession Bordereau Line (outbound)
views.description: The outbound cession bordereau, derived live from the canonical model: one line per policy premium movement ceded to a treaty, with the ceded amount computed from the contractual ceded share. This view - together with the data_dictionary - IS the bordereau: it is shared as a governed table, never exported to a spreadsheet.
views.grain: One row per ceded premium movement per policy per treaty.
views.sql:
SELECT
  tr.treaty_reference,
  DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', pt.transaction_date) AS reporting_month,
  p.policy_number,
  ins.name AS insured_name,
  p.line_of_business_code,
  p.inception_date,
  p.expiry_date,
  pt.currency_code,
  pt.amount AS gross_premium,
  ces.ceded_share,
  CAST(ROUND(pt.amount * ces.ceded_share, 2) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS ceded_premium
FROM {reinsurance.cession} ces
JOIN {policy.policy} p ON p.policy_id = ces.policy_id
JOIN {reinsurance.treaty} tr ON tr.treaty_id = ces.treaty_id
JOIN {policy.premium_transaction} pt ON pt.policy_id = p.policy_id
LEFT JOIN {party.party_role} pr
  ON pr.policy_id = p.policy_id AND pr.party_role_type_code = 'INSURED'
LEFT JOIN {party.party} ins ON ins.party_id = pr.party_id

views.name: vw_policy_current
views.title: Policy (current, derived)
views.description: Current policy state reconstructed from the version history - the projection that proves the event spine is complete. Selects exactly the columns of the policy table from the current version of each policy; it must reconcile row-for-row with policy. Consumers wanting "the policy as it is now" can read this or the policy table interchangeably; the audit truth is the event stream.
views.grain: One row per policy (its current version).
views.sql:
SELECT
  policy_id,
  policy_number,
  legal_entity_id,
  source_system_code,
  line_of_business_code,
  policy_status_code,
  inception_date,
  expiry_date,
  underwriting_year,
  currency_code,
  renews_policy_id
FROM {policy_lifecycle.policy_version}
WHERE is_current = TRUE

views.name: loss_development
views.title: Loss Development Triangle
views.description: The loss-development triangle as a governed view: for every accident year and development lag, the incremental and cumulative paid and incurred, derived by summation over claim transactions. Nothing is stored - the triangle is a semantic layer over claim.claim_transaction, so it always reconciles to the penny with the ledger and the claims sub-system. Accident year is the year of loss; development lag is transaction year minus accident year. Amounts are in original currency - group by or filter on currency_code before summing.
views.grain: One row per accident year per development lag per line of business per currency.
views.sql:
WITH movements AS (
  SELECT
    YEAR(c.loss_date)                                   AS accident_year,
    YEAR(ct.transaction_date) - YEAR(c.loss_date)       AS development_lag,
    p.line_of_business_code                             AS line_of_business_code,
    ct.currency_code                                    AS currency_code,
    ct.claim_transaction_type_code                      AS ttype,
    ct.amount                                           AS amount
  FROM {claim.claim_transaction} ct
  JOIN {claim.claim}  c ON c.claim_id  = ct.claim_id
  JOIN {policy.policy} p ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id
  WHERE YEAR(ct.transaction_date) >= YEAR(c.loss_date)
),
incremental AS (
  SELECT
    accident_year, development_lag, line_of_business_code, currency_code,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ttype IN ('INDEMNITY_PAYMENT','EXPENSE_PAYMENT') THEN amount
             WHEN ttype = 'RECOVERY' THEN amount ELSE 0 END)          AS incremental_paid,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ttype IN ('INDEMNITY_PAYMENT','EXPENSE_PAYMENT','RECOVERY','CASE_RESERVE_MOVEMENT')
             THEN amount ELSE 0 END)                                  AS incremental_incurred
  FROM movements
  GROUP BY accident_year, development_lag, line_of_business_code, currency_code
)
SELECT
  accident_year,
  development_lag,
  line_of_business_code,
  currency_code,
  incremental_paid,
  incremental_incurred,
  SUM(incremental_paid) OVER (
    PARTITION BY accident_year, line_of_business_code, currency_code
    ORDER BY development_lag ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS cumulative_paid,
  SUM(incremental_incurred) OVER (
    PARTITION BY accident_year, line_of_business_code, currency_code
    ORDER BY development_lag ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS cumulative_incurred
FROM incremental

views.name: financial_transaction
views.title: Financial Transaction (unified)
views.description: Unified view of all financial movements - premium and claim transactions - with their policy context, so portfolio metrics that span premium and claims (such as loss ratio) can be defined over a single source. Amounts are in original transaction currency.

SELECT

  p.underwriting_year,
  p.line_of_business_code,
  pt.currency_code,
  pt.transaction_date,
  'PREMIUM' AS transaction_kind,

  ct.currency_code,
  ct.transaction_date,

views.name: premium_earning
views.title: Premium Earning
views.description: Written, earned-to-date and unearned premium per policy, on a straight-line daily earning basis over the cover period. Honest limits: cancellations earn to their natural period in this version, and earning patterns other than straight-line are a later addition.
views.grain: One row per policy per currency with premium activity.
views.sql:
SELECT
  p.policy_id,
  p.line_of_business_code,
  p.underwriting_year,
  pt.currency_code,
  CAST(SUM(pt.amount) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS written_premium,
  CAST(SUM(pt.amount * LEAST(1.0, GREATEST(0.0,
      (datediff(LEAST(current_date(), p.expiry_date), p.inception_date) + 1) / 365.0)))
    AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS earned_premium,
  CAST(SUM(pt.amount) - SUM(pt.amount * LEAST(1.0, GREATEST(0.0,
      (datediff(LEAST(current_date(), p.expiry_date), p.inception_date) + 1) / 365.0)))
    AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS unearned_premium
FROM {policy.premium_transaction} pt
JOIN {policy.policy} p ON p.policy_id = pt.policy_id
GROUP BY p.policy_id, p.line_of_business_code, p.underwriting_year, pt.currency_code

views.name: underwriting_performance
views.title: Underwriting Performance Components
views.description: Earned premium, incurred claims and allocated expenses as one component stream, so ratio metrics (loss, expense, combined) are defined over a single source. Expenses are allocated at line level, not underwriting year.
views.grain: One row per component per line of business (per underwriting year where applicable) per currency.
views.sql:
SELECT line_of_business_code, underwriting_year, currency_code,
       'EARNED' AS component, earned_premium AS amount
FROM {semantics.premium_earning}
UNION ALL
SELECT p.line_of_business_code, p.underwriting_year, ct.currency_code,
       'INCURRED' AS component, ct.amount
FROM {claim.claim_transaction} ct
JOIN {claim.claim} c ON c.claim_id = ct.claim_id
JOIN {policy.policy} p ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id
UNION ALL
SELECT line_of_business_code, CAST(NULL AS BIGINT), currency_code,
       'EXPENSE' AS component, amount
FROM {finance.expense_transaction}

views.name: vw_premium_proof
views.title: Premium Proof (written = earned + unearned)
views.description: The premium reconciliation, by line of business and currency: written premium equals earned to date plus unearned (UPR). The residual must be zero - this is the proof that the earning engine conserves premium, shown as one number a controller can trust. Derived from the premium_earning view.
views.grain: One row per line of business per currency.
views.sql:
SELECT
  line_of_business_code,
  currency_code,
  CAST(SUM(written_premium) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS written_premium,
  CAST(SUM(earned_premium) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS earned_premium,
  CAST(SUM(unearned_premium) AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS unearned_premium,
  CAST(SUM(written_premium) - SUM(earned_premium) - SUM(unearned_premium)
    AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS residual
FROM {semantics.premium_earning}
GROUP BY line_of_business_code, currency_code

dimensions.name: currency_code
dimensions.description: Currency of the premiums. Group by this before summing money.

measures.description: The loss ratio: claims incurred over EARNED premium. This is the canonical, reporting-basis definition. (underwriting_metrics.loss_ratio_written is the quick written-basis view.) Meaningful within a single currency.

measures.name: expense_ratio
measures.expr: SUM(CASE WHEN component = 'EXPENSE' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN component = 'EARNED' THEN amount ELSE 0 END), 0)
measures.description: Expenses over earned premium.

measures.name: combined_ratio
measures.expr: (SUM(CASE WHEN component = 'INCURRED' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) + SUM(CASE WHEN component = 'EXPENSE' THEN amount ELSE 0 END)) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN component = 'EARNED' THEN amount ELSE 0 END), 0)
measures.description: Loss ratio plus expense ratio; below 1.0 is an underwriting profit.

measures.name: claims_paid
measures.expr: SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type_code IN ('INDEMNITY_PAYMENT', 'EXPENSE_PAYMENT') THEN amount ELSE 0 END)

functions.name: fn_claim_status
functions.description: One-line status of a claim - handling status, cause and loss date.

returns.description: status | cause | loss date, or NULL when unknown.

functions.sql:
(SELECT max(concat(claim_status_code, ' | ', cause_of_loss_code,
                   ' | loss date ', cast(loss_date AS STRING)))
 FROM {claim.claim} WHERE claim_number = in_claim_number)

functions.name: fn_outstanding_reserve
functions.description: The current outstanding case reserve on a claim, derived live as the sum of signed reserve movements - never a stored balance.

returns.description: Outstanding reserve in the claim currency; 0 when fully released.

functions.sql:
(SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ct.amount), 0)
 FROM {claim.claim_transaction} ct
 JOIN {claim.claim} c ON c.claim_id = ct.claim_id
 WHERE c.claim_number = in_claim_number
   AND ct.claim_transaction_type_code = 'CASE_RESERVE_MOVEMENT')

functions.name: fn_csm_closing
functions.description: The closing contractual service margin for a group of contracts, derived live as the signed sum of its CSM roll-forward movements - never a stored balance. The IFRS 17 reproducibility story in one call.

returns.description: Closing CSM in the group currency.

functions.name: fn_trial_balance_check
functions.description: The controller's first question, answered: does the ledger balance for a legal entity? Returns the net of all journal-line amounts - zero means debits equal credits.

returns.description: Net of all posting lines for the entity; 0.00 when the ledger balances.

functions.sql:
(SELECT COALESCE(SUM(jl.amount), 0)
 FROM {finance.journal_line} jl
 JOIN {finance.journal} j ON j.journal_id = jl.journal_id
 WHERE j.legal_entity_id = in_legal_entity_id)

functions.name: fn_champion_score
functions.description: The latest score from the champion model version for a given subject, derived live - never a stored balance. Lets any workbench ask 'what does the model in force say about this policy/quote/claim' without knowing which version that is.

inputs.name: in_subject_kind
inputs.description: Subject kind, one of POLICY, QUOTE, CLAIM, PARTY.

returns.description: Latest champion score for the subject; empty if none scored.

functions.sql:
(SELECT ms.score
 FROM {model.model_score} ms
 JOIN {model.model_version} mv ON mv.model_version_id = ms.model_version_id
 WHERE mv.model_status_code = 'CHAMPION'
   AND ms.subject_kind_code = in_subject_kind
   AND ms.subject_id = in_subject_id
 ORDER BY ms.scored_at DESC
 LIMIT 1)

functions.name: fn_earn_premium
functions.description: Earned premium to date for a policy, derived live on a straight-line daily basis over the cover period - never a stored balance. This is the governed earning engine: the same math the premium_earning view uses, callable per policy so any workbench earns premium the one agreed way.

inputs.name: in_policy_id
inputs.description: The policy to earn premium for.

returns.description: Gross earned premium to date in policy currency; 0 if none written.

functions.sql:
(SELECT CAST(COALESCE(SUM(pt.amount * LEAST(1.0, GREATEST(0.0,
      (datediff(LEAST(current_date(), p.expiry_date), p.inception_date) + 1) / 365.0))), 0)
    AS DECIMAL(18,2))
 FROM {policy.premium_transaction} pt
 JOIN {policy.policy} p ON p.policy_id = pt.policy_id
 WHERE pt.policy_id = in_policy_id)

functions.name: fn_policy_snapshot
functions.description: One-line snapshot of a policy - line, status, cover period, year, currency.

returns.description: lob | status | period | underwriting year | currency, or NULL when unknown.

functions.sql:
(SELECT max(concat(line_of_business_code, ' | ', policy_status_code, ' | ',
                   cast(inception_date AS STRING), ' to ', cast(expiry_date AS STRING),
                   ' | uwy ', cast(underwriting_year AS STRING), ' | ', currency_code))
 FROM {policy.policy} WHERE policy_number = in_policy_number)

functions.name: fn_verify_event_chain
functions.description: Verifies the hash chain of a policy's event stream, live - returns the number of broken events (0 means intact). An event is broken if its stored hash does not equal the hash recomputed from its fields chained onto the prior event's hash, or if its prior-hash link does not match the actual previous event. This makes "prove nothing was edited" a query, not a claim. The canonical hashed fields are the structured identity - policy_id, sequence_no, event type and effective_from (free text is deliberately excluded so the check is deterministic).

inputs.name: in_policy_id
inputs.description: The policy whose event chain to verify.

returns.description: Count of broken events in the chain; 0 if the chain is intact.

functions.sql:
(SELECT COUNT(*)
 FROM {policy_lifecycle.policy_event} e
 LEFT JOIN {policy_lifecycle.policy_event} p
   ON p.policy_id = e.policy_id AND p.sequence_no = e.sequence_no - 1
 WHERE e.policy_id = in_policy_id
   AND (
     e.event_hash <> sha2(concat(coalesce(e.prior_event_hash, ''),
       concat_ws('|', e.policy_id, cast(e.sequence_no AS STRING),
                 e.policy_event_type_code, cast(e.effective_from AS STRING))), 256)
     OR coalesce(e.prior_event_hash, '') <> coalesce(p.event_hash, '')
   ))

functions.name: fn_appetite_check
functions.description: Checks a prospective risk against the live appetite rules and returns the effect (WITHIN_APPETITE, REFER or OUT_OF_APPETITE) with the matching rule's business description. The same rules humans read; the tool agents call before quoting.

inputs.name: in_lob
inputs.description: Line of business code, e.g. COMMERCIAL_PROPERTY.

inputs.name: in_country
inputs.description: Country code of the risk, e.g. GB.

inputs.name: in_sum_insured
inputs.description: Proposed sum insured in the product currency.

returns.description: effect | rule description, or a REFER fallback when no rule matches.

functions.sql:
COALESCE(
  (SELECT min_by(concat(appetite_effect_code, ' | ', description), rule_order)
   FROM {product.appetite_rule}
   WHERE line_of_business_code = in_lob
     AND (country_code IS NULL OR country_code = in_country)
     AND (max_sum_insured IS NULL OR in_sum_insured <= max_sum_insured)
     AND effective_from <= current_date()
     AND (effective_to IS NULL OR effective_to >= current_date())),
  'REFER | no matching appetite rule - refer to underwriting')

functions.name: fn_indicative_quote
functions.description: Returns an indicative gross premium for an active product and sum insured, from the product's declared base rate. Indicative only - binding terms always pass through an underwriting decision.

inputs.name: in_sum_insured
inputs.description: Proposed sum insured in the product currency.

returns.description: Indicative gross premium; NULL when the product is unknown or inactive.

functions.sql:
round((SELECT max(base_rate)
       FROM {product.product}
       WHERE product_code = in_product_code
         AND product_status_code = 'ACTIVE') * in_sum_insured, 2)

functions.name: fn_define
functions.description: Looks a business term up in the data dictionary - the model explaining itself to humans and agents alike.

inputs.name: in_term
inputs.description: An entity or attribute name, e.g. loss_ratio or claim.

returns.description: Up to three matching definitions, '||'-separated; NULL when unknown.

functions.sql:
(SELECT array_join(slice(sort_array(collect_list(
          concat(entity_name, '.', attribute_name, ': ', definition))), 1, 3), ' || ')
 FROM {reference.data_dictionary}
 WHERE lower(attribute_name) = lower(in_term) OR lower(entity_name) = lower(in_term))

functions.name: fn_cession_trace
functions.description: Which treaties a policy is ceded to, and at what shares.

returns.description: Semicolon-separated 'treaty @ share' list; NULL when nothing is ceded.

functions.sql:
(SELECT array_join(sort_array(collect_list(
          concat(t.treaty_reference, ' @ ', cast(ces.ceded_share AS STRING)))), '; ')
 FROM {reinsurance.cession} ces
 JOIN {policy.policy} p ON p.policy_id = ces.policy_id
 JOIN {reinsurance.treaty} t ON t.treaty_id = ces.treaty_id
 WHERE p.policy_number = in_policy_number)
